panel.title: How to read this dashboard
panel.p.role: This screen is not a trading tool and never says "buy" or "sell". It says where to look first, and why. Each list is a hypothesis under observation, not a recommendation.
panel.p.frozen: The entry rules of each list were written down, quantified and frozen BEFORE the first observation, together with their success criteria. That is the only way to avoid telling yourself a story after the fact: adjusting a threshold because you have seen the result amounts to rigging an exam already handed in. Changing any rule resets the observation clock to zero.
panel.p.families: The two washout lists ask the same question — is this stock marked down for no reason of its own? — with two different signatures: one looks at a general market decline, the other at a fall that happens in complete indifference. The Rocket and Phoenix profiles ask an entirely different question, with relative thresholds recomputed every day. No crossing of these two worlds has ever been measured: that is why no profile badge appears on the washout lists.
panel.p.survivors: Every historical figure shown is measured on the past, and on companies still listed today only: bankruptcies have vanished from the data, which necessarily makes those figures optimistic. Treat them as a ceiling of hope, never as a promise.
panel.p.forward: The only judge is the live tracking further down the page: each qualifying stock is recorded the very same day, at that day's price, then followed until the end of its observation window. Those results, and those alone, will settle the question.
panel.p.checkpoint: The checkpoint shown in the tracking table is an intermediate reading, never a sell order: systematically cutting the stocks that lag destroys the measured return of the whole set, because a large share of the strongest rises was still going through a negative phase at that stage.
gloss.beta: Sensitivity of the stock to the market: beta 1.6 = when the small-cap index moves −1%, this stock moves −1.6% on average.
gloss.ruleDil: No document preparing an issuance of new shares filed with the US regulator in the last 180 days: a pending issuance crushes the price when it lands.
gloss.phenix: A massacred stock, far from its yearly high, whose moves are calming down and which shows the first signs of stabilization.
gloss.fusee: A stock already on fire: among the strongest risers of the day, over three months and over one month at once.
gloss.dilution: The company filed a document preparing an issuance of new shares: your stake will be reduced and the arrival of the shares crushes the price.
gloss.prelist: Stocks that pass the per-stock rules but are waiting for the market condition to be met.
research.badge: Statistical research — live observation in progress
research.tip: This list applies a hypothesis drawn from the past whose promise is not demonstrated: it is under full-scale observation.

market.section.title: Market washout
market.intro: This list only activates on days when the small-cap market as a whole declines: when everything falls at once, stocks get marked down without anything having happened to them in particular. On rising days it stays empty, and that is the expected behaviour — not a malfunction. The display order follows the stock's own fall: the share of its decline that the market's decline does not explain.
market.rule.chg: Deep enough fall over about a month
market.note.benchmark_missing: Market state unavailable → no list today.
market.note.market_bullish: Bullish market (IWM {w} d {pct}) → the method does not apply.
market.note.error: List unavailable today — the rest of the scan is intact.
market.emptyInfo: The absence of a list is information, not a malfunction: the method only looks during general sell-offs.
market.disclaimer: Figures measured on the past, companies still listed only, thresholds picked after the fact — a ceiling of hope, not a promise. Judgement will come from the real results observed live. Not investment advice.
market.buy.title: Before any purchase
market.buy.body: : read the recent filings (the catalyst is in the news, not in our figures) · check the bid/ask spread (if it is 3%, you need +3% just to break even) · size the position to survive −50%.
quiet.section.title: Quiet washout — {w} d window
quiet.intro: Same idea, different signature: a stock collapsing in complete indifference — no surge in volume, no money fleeing — looks like a mechanical oversold move rather than a deserved shipwreck. The same measurement is observed over three durations declared in advance and published together: none of them is "the right one", the short ones see the flash purges the long one misses, and vice versa.
quiet.rule.mkt: Market declining over the same window
quiet.rule.flow: Money flow not clearly on the sell side

tracking.title: Tracking of qualifying stocks
tracking.subtitle: position against the trajectories measured on the past — information, never a sell order
tracking.empty: No stock recorded yet — waiting for the first bearish market. The journal started on July 6, 2026; each daily scan records its list, empty or not.
tracking.calendar: Observation schedule: checkpoint on day {cp}, close on day {h} — trading days counted from entry.
tracking.notAnExit: The checkpoint is not an exit. A stock that falls below the threshold stays under observation until the close: cutting the laggards along the way destroys the measured return of the whole basket, because a large share of the strongest winners is still in negative territory at that stage.
tracking.noOpen: No stock under observation today: every recorded row has completed its window.
perf.title: Real results of the selections
perf.subtitle: measured live, with nothing erased — this is the table that will decide
perf.intro: Every stock that shows up in a scan is recorded the same day, at that day's price, then tracked until today. The list of selections is frozen in advance and never rewritten afterwards: that is what sets these figures apart from the ones measured on the past, where the companies that disappeared were erased from the data. A stock whose prices are no longer published drops out of the tracked count — the gap between the two numbers below measures it.
perf.counts: {tracked} stocks tracked out of {picks} recorded · last measured {when}
perf.frame.fast: What this tracking will settle quickly: the average gain. A few dozen rows are enough to see which way the whole basket leans against the index — not to know the exact figure, but enough to tell whether the method adds or destroys return.
perf.frame.slow: What it will not settle for years: how often stocks double. Roughly one small cap in fifty doubles within a quarter, across the board; showing that a compartment beats that base rate takes hundreds of closed rows. Until then, the last two columns read as anecdotes, never as a rate.
perf.frame.verdict: The verdict on the extreme zones is already in: the Rocket / Phoenix hypothesis was tested against success criteria written in advance, and refuted in July 2026. This table does not re-judge it criterion by criterion — it measures what was actually selected. It is the only result that could one day contradict that verdict, and doing so will take time and a clear gap.
perf.note.overlap: One stock can carry both profiles: the compartments do not add up.
perf.note.unknown: "Recorded before the profiles": rows from scans older than the two profiles. Their compartment is unknown and will stay that way — they still count in the whole basket.
perf.empty: No selection tracked yet. The table fills itself as the daily scans accumulate: a stock enters on the day it first appears, and never leaves.
perf.unavailable: Real results temporarily unavailable. The tracking keeps running server-side; the rest of the page is up to date.
zones.title: 🔥🚀 Extreme zones — to study, not to buy
zones.intro: These two profiles come from an earlier hypothesis: spotting the stocks sitting at the extremes of the day's distribution, where exploration saw the strongest rises concentrate. It was tested once and for all in July 2026, with its success criteria written in advance, and it was refuted: doublings are indeed far more frequent there, so are collapses, and the measured average gain stays negative in both cases. The profiles remain on screen because they select the pool shown here and because they are material for human research — never a buy list.

footer.trace.title: Traceability
footer.trace.body: : every figure displayed is served by the API from tables frozen before observation — nothing invented, nothing recomputed live. All terms:
flag.binary_event: Biotech / pharma — binary events: technical signals are unreliable here
flag.earnings_soon: Earnings in {d} d — a move may come from that, not from the setup
risk.going_concern: Official doubt about the company's ability to keep operating
risk.sub_dollar: Price below the listing floor, {n} sessions in a row
risk.tip.going_concern: In their official report, the auditor writes that they doubt the company will survive twelve months: it is the most direct accounting signal of distress there is.
risk.tip.reverse_split: The company reduced the number of shares outstanding to mechanically lift its price — most often in order to stay listed.
risk.tip.dilution: A document preparing an issuance of new shares has been filed: your stake will be reduced. Read it against the line of business — a company with no revenue yet funds itself this way as a matter of course, so the fact is frequent there and does not say the same thing as elsewhere.
risk.tip.late_filing: The quarterly or annual report was not filed on time and the company declared it: internal disorder, or disagreement with the auditor.
risk.tip.sub_dollar: The price stayed below the floor required by the listing venue for several sessions in a row. Past a certain duration, the company receives a non-compliance notice.
